pr_title: kubectl/pkg/cmd/describe: cache describers to reuse clients
pr_body:
Signed-off-by: Andrew Keesler <akeesler@vmware.com>

/sig cli

**What type of PR is this?**

/kind cleanup

**What this PR does / why we need it**:

- Previously, during `kubectl describe`, we were creating a `kubernetes.Clientset` per object to describe, which is unnecessary.
- See https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/91913#issuecomment-646291219 for numerical evidence.

**Which issue(s) this PR fixes**:

(Partially) fixes #91913.

**Special notes for your reviewer**:

- Read https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/91913#issuecomment-646291219 and onward to learn the backstory for this issue.

- This bug is related to the client-go credential plugin feature set, which is tracked here: https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/issues/541.
- The feature set is currently in beta, and we want to get it to GA, which involves tackling the related bugs.
- See https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/91913#issuecomment-646291219 and onward for why this bug is related to the client-go credential plugin feature set.

**Does this PR introduce a user-facing change?**:

issue_context.title: kubectl output flooded with warnings about aws-iam-authenticator
issue_context.body:
**What happened**:
`kubectl -A describe pods`

Results in a flood of messages like:
`W0608 10:47:22.221620   25245 exec.go:203] constructing many client instances from the same exec auth config can cause performance problems during cert rotation and can exhaust available network connections; 3825 clients constructed calling "aws-iam-authenticator"`

**What you expected to happen**:

No warnings.

**How to reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)**:
In an EKS environment where aws-iam-authenticator is used to get tokens:
```
users:
- name: myuser
  user:
    exec:
      apiVersion: client.authentication.k8s.io/v1alpha1
      args:
      - token
      - -i
      - dev
      command: aws-iam-authenticator
      env:
      - name: AWS_PROFILE
        value: dev
```

**Anything else we need to know?**:

**Environment**:
- Kubernetes version (use `kubectl version`):
```
Client Version: version.Info{Major:"1", Minor:"18", GitVersion:"v1.18.2", GitCommit:"52c56ce7a8272c798dbc29846288d7cd9fbae032", GitTreeState:"clean", BuildDate:"2020-04-16T23:34:25Z", GoVersion:"go1.14.2", Compiler:"gc", Platform:"darwin/amd64"}
Server Version: version.Info{Major:"1", Minor:"16+", GitVersion:"v1.16.8-eks-e16311", GitCommit:"e163110a04dcb2f39c3325af96d019b4925419eb", GitTreeState:"clean", BuildDate:"2020-03-27T22:37:12Z", GoVersion:"go1.13.8", Compiler:"gc", Platform:"linux/amd64"}
```
- Cloud provider or hardware configuration: EKS
- OS (e.g: `cat /etc/os-release`): macos
- Kernel (e.g. `uname -a`): Darwin Kernel Version 19.5.0

> is describe constructing a new client per described object

this seems to be the case (i wrote my stream of consciousness notes below). i am having trouble understanding why we need a new client per described object...do you have any historical context here/thoughts of why this would be the case?

---

1. for each of the `pods`, we create a `describe.ResourceDescriber`: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/aa348b15770e27df927203bb7cac8c154b42c44f/staging/src/k8s.io/kubectl/pkg/cmd/describe/describe.go#L179
2. for each `describe.ResourceDescriber`, we create a `*kubernetes.Clientset`: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/aa348b15770e27df927203bb7cac8c154b42c44f/staging/src/k8s.io/kubectl/pkg/describe/describe.go#L160
3. for each `*kubernetes.Clientset`, we create a client for each API version: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/aa348b15770e27df927203bb7cac8c154b42c44f/staging/src/k8s.io/client-go/kubernetes/clientset.go#L370
4. for each API version client, we create a `*rest.RESTClient`: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/aa348b15770e27df927203bb7cac8c154b42c44f/staging/src/k8s.io/client-go/kubernetes/typed/apps/v1/apps_client.go#L67
5. upon creation, a `*rest.RESTClient` transitively calls `exec.Authenticator.UpdateTransportConfig()`: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/aa348b15770e27df927203bb7cac8c154b42c44f/staging/src/k8s.io/client-go/plugin/pkg/client/auth/exec/exec.go#L203

my estimation is that the number of times that `exec.Authenticator.UpdateTransportConfig()` is called is `O(nm)` where `n` is the number of `pods` and `m` is the number of per-API version clients.

i count 41 per-API version clients in a `*kubernetes.Clientset`. when i have 36 pods, i see the warning message show up for 1515 clients. 36 * 41 = 1476 which is close enough to 1515 to make me think that the above estimation is correct.

I do not think there is any way for `UpdateTransportConfig` to know when the associated client is no longer needed (and I do no think we can ignore the input `c.Dial` in an attempt to share a single dialer across all clients).  That is, `onRotateList` grows without bound and we "leak" clients.  A bandage solution would be to cache the `describer` based on the `mapping` (in a function local map):

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/aa348b15770e27df927203bb7cac8c154b42c44f/staging/src/k8s.io/kubectl/pkg/cmd/describe/describe.go#L178-L179

This is a one-off solution for describe, and does not help in the general case of "bad things happen when you make too many clients and immediately throw them away."

In an ideal world we would be able to make as many clients as we want because we cache the underlying transport in `tlsCache`.

> this seems to be the case (i wrote my stream of consciousness notes below)

nice investigation, thanks!

> A bandage solution would be to cache the `describer` based on the `mapping` (in a function local map)

We should do *something* to improve describe (even if we're also able to improve the tlsCache hits)... constructing 1500 clients to describe 40 pods is egregious, and just figuring out the inputs to determine a tlsCache hit is more expensive than I'd want to pay 1500 times.

> This is a one-off solution for describe, and does not help in the general case of "bad things happen when you make too many clients and immediately throw them away."
> 
> In an ideal world we would be able to make as many clients as we want because we cache the underlying transport in `tlsCache`.

I agree it would be good to improve this, though the ability to compare opaque inputs for cache-hit purposes is limited.
Seems like a least common denominator here is to fix the describe behavior so that it doesn't create so many clients. I'll try to see if I can improve on that for starters.

I also face this problem when using `kubectl get` with certain output formats (`yaml`, `json`, `name`, etc) whenever there are more than 1000 items in the response. The default and `wide` formats do not exhibit the problem.

```
$ kubectl get -A serviceaccounts -o yaml                         
W0824 10:26:28.583521    9831 exec.go:203] constructing many client instances from the same exec auth config can cause performance problems during cert rotation and can exhaust available network connections; 1001 clients constructed calling "aws"
W0824 10:26:28.583731    9831 exec.go:203] constructing many client instances from the same exec auth config can cause performance problems during cert rotation and can exhaust available network connections; 1002 clients constructed calling "aws"
W0824 10:26:28.583834    9831 exec.go:203] constructing many client instances from the same exec auth config can cause performance problems during cert rotation and can exhaust available network connections; 1003 clients constructed calling "was"
...
```

```
$ kubectl version
Client Version: version.Info{Major:"1", Minor:"18", GitVersion:"v1.18.8", GitCommit:"9f2892aab98fe339f3bd70e3c470144299398ace", GitTreeState:"clean", BuildDate:"2020-08-13T16:12:48Z", GoVersion:"go1.13.15", Compiler:"gc", Platform:"darwin/amd64"}
Server Version: version.Info{Major:"1", Minor:"17+", GitVersion:"v1.17.9-eks-4c6976", GitCommit:"4c6976793196d70bc5cd29d56ce5440c9473648e", GitTreeState:"clean", BuildDate:"2020-07-17T18:46:04Z", GoVersion:"go1.13.9", Compiler:"gc", Platform:"linux/amd64"}
```
cc @micahhausler

@orirawlings @mikedanese I also see this when using `kubectl get` where there are a large number of objects returned
e.g. 
```
$ kubectl get jobs -o json
...
W1207 13:58:33.030725    2207 exec.go:203] constructing many client instances from the same exec auth config can cause performance problems during cert rotation and can exhaust available network connections; 2266 clients constructed calling "aws"
...
```

I was able to reproduce that `get` behavior. I created around 1000-ish (1094 to be exact) `configmaps` in a single namespace, ran `kubectl get configmaps -o yaml`, and saw those warning messages.

---

Currently I partition this GH issue up into 3-ish chunks, in order from most egregious to least egregious:
1. `kubernetes/staging/src/k8s.io/kubectl/pkg/cmd/describe/describe.go` should not be creating a client for every object it wants to describe
1. `In an ideal world we would be able to make as many clients as we want because we cache the underlying transport in tlsCache` (from @enj's comment[0] above)
1. `get` should not be creating a client for every object it wants to print out (I didn't actually see this in the code, but it does seem like this is what is causing those warnings to show up when dealing with 1000+ objects)

- For `#1`, I feel like we could implement the bandage solution @enj suggested above (i.e., function-local cache of `describe.ResourceDescriber`) since this would be a net improvement on the `describe` code. I will open a PR to do that.
- For `#2`, I am still scratching my head, because coming up with a cache key for this seems hard (a la @liggitt's) note above[1]. I will focus on `#1` for now and then come back to this one.
- For `#3`, I wonder if we could do something similar to what we do for `#1`. I will open up a fix for `#1`, have it go through review, get it merged in, and then figure out if we want to generalize the fix to work for `#3`. I feel like we should fix `#2` before we fix `#3`, though, since `#2` is the root of the evil.

[0] https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/91913#issuecomment-646395427
[1] https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/91913#issuecomment-648898361

> 2\. `In an ideal world we would be able to make as many clients as we want because we cache the underlying transport in tlsCache` (from @enj's comment[0] above)

Anything that customizes a function in rest.Config is uncacheable (see https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/95427), so rapidly creating lots of clients from a config is still not great
Opened a PR for `#1`: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/97811.

> Currently I partition this GH issue up into 3-ish chunks

from the earlier analysis:

> for each *kubernetes.Clientset, we create a client for each API version

that also seems like a distinct issue to improve on

Status:
1. superfluous describe clients, `pr opened`: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/97811
1. creating >1000 clients means you start to get spammed with warnings, `in progress`[0]
1. superfluous get clients, `in progress`[1]
1. for each *kubernetes.Clientset we create a client for each API version `in progress` (from @liggitt's comment above)

[0] strawperson proposal: do nothing
- i thought about this all afternoon yesterday, and i feel like since we want 1) our exec plugin code to be able to close connections for those clients when certificates rotate (which seems absolutely necessary from a system resource perspective) and 2) a 1:many relationship between `exec.Authenticator`'s and clients (which seems desired from a memory usage perspective and synchronization perspective), and 3) we want to abstract our `exec.Authenticator` `RoundTripper` code from underlying L4 details, then we are stuck with this problem of needing to keep an ever growing list of connection information
- the more i think about this, the more i think that the real issue here is that we are creating >1000 clients in some places
- 1000 clients is a lot - seems like this should only be necessary when you have 1000 distinct API endpoints that need some sort of network isolation (e.g., flow control)
- to my knowledge, kube does not have 1000 distinct API endpoints that would need individual clients

[1] strawperson proposal: reuse same `rest.RESTClient` for each `schema.GroupVersion`

Important note! User facing behavior change!

- In this proposed change, we would be using the same `kubernetes.Clientset` to describe each individual resource in `infos`.
- That means that rate limiting will take effect.
- When running on my machine with a `kind` cluster and 100 `ConfigMaps`'s, `kubectl describe cm 1>/dev/null 2>/dev/null` slows down from about `1.5s` to `38s`. :(
- Although! We already see this rate limiting take effect with the `kubectl describe cm some-prefix-` behavior (i.e., `describe.DescribeMatchingResources`), so maybe rate limiting in both cases is more congruent behavior.
- Regardless, this seems like a user-facing change, so I wanted to point this out.
- I don't feel great about this slowdown, even with the benefit that this change brings.
- I tried increasing the `QPS`/`Burst` on the client, but that seemed arbitrary and janky.
- I am curious of other people's thoughts here.

> * When running on my machine with a `kind` cluster and 100 `ConfigMaps`'s, `kubectl describe cm 1>/dev/null 2>/dev/null` slows down from about `1.5s` to `38s`. :(

What's really unfortunate is that we've already fetched the objects from the server using a list call... ideally, we would just describe the object we fetched directly rather than re-fetching it

Yeah, agreed. I was just taking a peek at that. Since we also (optionally) print out events associated with the object that we are describing, I believe we will need to make some sort of API call. However, if we reused the `info.Object` that would get rid of 1 API call...

When I make a code change to pass the `info.Object` directly to the `ConfigMapDescriber` and run the same test as I did above with 100 `ConfigMap`'s, I get a runtime of about `18s`. Improvement. The need for the searching of `Event`'s is still adding an order of magnitude, though.

My gut says to spin this improvement out into another GH issue.
